conventions.convention: Assume AC. The likelihood ratio is dP1/dP0; the restrictions of P0 and P1 are equivalent at every finite time, including time zero. Density representatives are nonnegative and measurable.
Testing starts at t=1. Thresholds α,β belong to (0,1); L_t≥1/α decides H1 and L_t≤β decides H0. The infimum of an empty crossing set is infinity, with no finite terminal decision.
IID means mutual independence under each law. Factorization requires only Q1 absolutely continuous with respect to Q0 and uses the observation-generated finite-time sigma-algebras.

Termination uses equivalent coordinate laws, finite absolute log-likelihood means under both laws, strictly negative drift under Q0 and strictly positive drift under Q1, with trivial initial sigma-algebra.

load_bearing.statement: For equivalent finite-time restrictions, inspect likelihood-ratio representatives at t=1,2,…; stop and decide H1 at L_t≥1/α, otherwise stop and decide H0 at L_t≤β, otherwise continue. An infinite stopping time has no finite terminal decision.

Assume AC. For random elements IID under each P_j with coordinate laws Q_j, Q1 absolutely continuous with respect to Q0, and nonnegative representative λ=dQ1/dQ0, the product L_t=∏_{i=1}^t λ(X_i) is a version of d(P1 restricted to F_t)/d(P0 restricted to F_t), where F_t=σ(X1,…,Xt), for every t≥1.
Assume AC. Under the algorithm's hypotheses, τ is a stopping time and P0(τ<∞, L_τ≥1/α)≤α and P1(τ<∞, L_τ≤β)≤β, without assuming almost-sure termination.

Assume AC. For observations IID under each P_j with equivalent coordinate laws Q_j, choose finite strictly positive λ=dQ1/dQ0 and put Z=log λ. If both absolute Z means are finite and E_Q0 Z<0<E_Q1 Z, then for every α,β∈(0,1), the algorithm on the observation filtration with trivial F0 satisfies P0(τ<∞)=P1(τ<∞)=1.

concerns.concern: The proof needs an explicit null-set qualification for arbitrary density representatives. Step 4.1 applies the real-valued test-supermartingale supplier directly to L, although the algorithm permits nonnegative RN representatives that may equal infinity on measurable null sets. Step 5.1 also says the terminal H0 event 'is contained in' the reciprocal crossing event, but R_t was set to zero where L_t=0, so this containment holds only outside a P1-null set. Replacing infinite values by finite values at each time for the Ville application and taking the countable union of exceptional sets closes both points without changing either error bound.
